body:
Seems like we had this issue before with copy_from as well:

https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/69349

I am experiencing this issue as well. Talked it out with the community: https://elasticstack.slack.com/archives/CNTP6NLTZ/p1641779140142600

Would very much like to be able to get this fixed. :) Good find!!!
Good find @original-brownbear! This is a very sneaky bug. I think the enrich processor should make a deep copy of the _source before inserting it to the IngestDocument.

> I think the enrich processor should make a deep copy of the _source before inserting it to the IngestDocument.

Sounds good. Additionally we could also look into making whatever we store in the cache immutable to prevent this kind of bug going forward (also looks like we could get away with storing just the search hit map and not the full search hit). Just some thoughts.

> Additionally we could also look into making whatever we store in the cache immutable to prevent this kind of bug going forward

+1, we should try to recursively wrap the _source in an immutable map when adding a cache entry.

> also looks like we could get away with storing just the search hit map and not the full search hit)

Yes, this makes sense. The value of cache should be `List<Map<?, ?>>`, in case multiple hits were returned.

issue.body:
The enrich cache currently uses `SearchResponse` as cache value,
which contains the hits used by the enrich processor for enrichment.
What is actually used is by the enrich processor is `SearchHit.getSourceAsMap()`,
which is a map of maps representation of a search hit.

The problem is that this map is mutable and the map of maps is directly
passed into `IngestDocument` and at the same time this is cached by the
enrich cache via `SearchResponse` cache value. Any processor that modifies
the content added by the enrich processor, also changes the map of maps
representation of a search hit in the cache. This corrupts the cache,
because if this the enrich cache serves a cache entry for the same key,
a different snippet added to the document being enriched.

The following changes have been made to fix this bug:
* Use `List<Map<?, ?>>` as cache value for the enrich cache.
* Upon caching lookup / search, make an immutable deep copy of `SearchHit.getSourceAsMap()`.
* Upon serving an entry from the cache, make a normal deep copy,
  so the enrichent can be safely modified by subsequent processors.

Closes #82340
